offlineProtection.explainerLead: During the service, the dashboard or kitchen screen must be on and online.
offlineProtection.explainerBody: If the screen turns off, the device loses the internet or you switch to another website, offline protection takes over — it pauses orders or turns off auto-accept, whichever you chose.
offlineProtection.reminder: ⚠️ Keep the dashboard or kitchen screen on and online during the service, otherwise offline protection may take over.
offlineProtection.enableConfirm:
Offline protection is on.

For orders to keep arriving, the screen must stay on. If this device loses connection, offline protection takes over in the mode you chose.

Check that “Screen on” is switched on on this device.
offlineProtection.disableConfirm:
Turn off offline protection for this event?

If this device loses connection, online orders will continue — customers may send orders you won’t see. Turn it off only if you have a reliable connection.
offlineProtection.cardDescription: Decides what happens to incoming orders when your device is left without a connection.
offlineProtection.purpose: If your device loses its connection, this stops orders arriving while you can’t see them.
offlineProtection.switchHelp: What happens when this van loses its connection.
offlineProtection.modes.pause.label: Pause online orders
offlineProtection.modes.pause.help: Customers can’t order until you’re back online.
offlineProtection.modes.no_auto_accept.l: Keep taking orders, confirm them yourself
offlineProtection.modes.no_auto_accept.h: Auto-accept is turned off, so customers can still order but nothing is confirmed automatically. You’ll confirm each order when you’re back online — and anything still waiting is rejected automatically after the time you chose, and the customer gets an email letting them know.
kitchenCapacity.desc: The largest number of items your kitchen can prepare at once, across all the categories you’ve ticked. Each category’s batch size still applies on top.
kitchenCapacity.example: Example: if you can cook 4 mains in 5 minutes, set 4 items every 5 minutes. Total capacity limits orders across all selected categories, so if you want to sell at most 10 starters and mains every 5 minutes, set “Total capacity” to 10 items every 5 minutes and tick “Starters” and “Mains”. Mains will still stay limited to 4 items every 5 minutes.
kitchenCapacity.noLimit: Leave the infinity sign for no limit.
kitchenCapacity.warning: ⚠️ For kitchen capacity to work properly, set a prep time and batch size in the menu categories (“Menu & Stock”). Without them, capacity can’t know how long items take to cook.
kitchenCapacity.noVan: Add a van in Settings › Van settings to set your kitchen capacity.
kitchenCapacity.lead: How many items your kitchen can prepare, so customers can only pick collection times you can meet.
kitchenCapacity.sameForAll: The same kitchen capacity for all vans?
kitchenCapacity.confirmBody: All vans will use the same kitchen capacity as {van}. Each van’s numbers will be replaced.
kitchenCapacity.colCountsTitle: Which categories count toward total capacity. Cooked categories always count; tick the instant categories (sides, dips, drinks) to include them.

settingsCopy.allowCancellation.label: Allow customers to cancel orders
settingsCopy.allowCancellation.sentence: Customers can cancel at the latest <select></select> before the pickup time
settingsCopy.autoAccept.label: Auto-accept orders
settingsCopy.autoAccept.help: Orders confirm automatically. If the requested slot is full, the order moves to the next free slot. It only confirms when there is capacity. Orders with customer notes (e.g. an allergy) still have to be confirmed manually.
settingsCopy.orderReady.label: “The order is ready” step
settingsCopy.orderReady.help: Shows a “Mark as ready” button on the orders screen. Kitchen screens are set separately, on each device. Customers get an email whenever an order is marked as ready. Applies to all events — you can still turn it on or off for a single event on its dashboard.
settingsCopy.buzzers.label: Do you hand out buzzers for pickup?
settingsCopy.buzzers.help: Record which buzzer you gave each customer, so you know who to look for when the food is ready.
settingsCopy.buzzers.countLabel: How many buzzers do you have?
whereYouTrade.stepHeading: Where is your food truck based?
whereYouTrade.stepIntro: This sets the currency, prices, time zone and phone number format. The country can’t be changed later, because it is tied to card payments.
whereYouTrade.countryGuessed: We guessed this from where you are. Change it if it’s wrong.
whereYouTrade.townQuestion: Town or city where you are based
whereYouTrade.saveFailed: The settings couldn’t be saved — try again.
stockCopy.defaultScopeNote: Default for every event. To set a different amount for one event, change it on that event’s dashboard — events you’ve already set there keep their own amount.

managePrimitives.allergenMode.cardBody: Upload or paste a single allergen card (PDF, image or text), shown as it is. Per-dish tags stay hidden.

manageSettings.schedule.title: Your schedule
manageSettings.schedule.autoDesc: Tell us where you publish the schedule and we’ll check it for you, sending you the events we find for approval. This must be your own website — not a Facebook or Instagram page.
manageSettings.schedule.eitherWay: Either way, if we find your events published elsewhere, we’ll still send them to you for approval. Nothing is published until you confirm it.
